summary_for_children: At-Takathur warns that competing for more distracts people until they reach the graves.
environment_concept: Towers of crates, jars and boxes stacked higher and higher beside the path, each trying to outgrow the last (102:1). Further on, a quiet walled graveyard with plain, unmarked stones (102:2). No person is shown. The Day of Judgement and the Fire are not pictured.
architecture_and_scenery: Stacked crate towers, a low graveyard wall with a gate, plain upright stones.

areas.name: The Quiet Graveyard
areas.description: A walled graveyard with plain stones. A calm place to remember that this life ends.

unique_world.visual_theme: A busy town market on a bright morning with stalls heaped high under a string of bunting

primary_mechanic.text: At four stalls, buy exactly what the household list says (4 loaves, 6 eggs, 1 jar of oil, 2 bunches of dates) while each stallholder calls out to buy more than the neighbours; too few is refused (someone goes without) and more is refused as piling up (102:1).

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading at the market gate, the shopping list, then a reading on the way home
world_assets: four stalls with crates heaped high
environment_behaviour: a basket appears at each stall once its goods are bought
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that competing to pile up more distracts us, and we will be asked about blessings (102:1, 102:8)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Race for More
story_library.children_narration: Imagine always wanting one more toy, one more prize, or one more treasure. Would having more things automatically make us happy? Surah At-Takathur warns us about becoming so distracted by competing for possessions that we forget what really matters.

world_idea.title: The Tower of Treasures
world_idea.description: Explore a whimsical tower full of objects, then discover that possessions cannot replace gratitude, responsibility, and kindness.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
